items.title: Randy Weston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So she arranged for myself, and three Gnawa from Tangiers and leaders from everywhere. So it was my first experience to be in Canterbury... We had to play for them.

ctx.x: Mandrill, and Pucho and His Latin Soul Brothers, and we had 40 African musicians. We had this three-day festival at a bullring in Tangiers. Two nights it was at the bullring and the next night it was a Sahara sandstorm coming from the Sahara. We couldn’t play in the bull right so we had to rush and clean up this theatre called Theatre Cervantes in Tangiers. That was an experience, and I having that club, that was an experience. We had a blues band from Chicago sometime. We had singers from the Congo…we played…
You have an experience with the Arch Bishop of Canterbury, talk about that.
Well, that was organized by a woman from India, Zeba…
